strings.name: Daniel Ek
strings.summary: Ek co-founded Spotify with Martin Lorentzon, helping shift music from downloads to ad-supported and subscription streaming. The company later expanded into podcasts and audiobooks, amid debate over royalties, creator income and layoffs. His investment firm’s defense-technology financing also prompted artist protests. In 2026 he moved from CEO to executive chairman, focusing on long-term strategy and capital allocation.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Spotify and popularized music-streaming subscriptions, changing digital music consumption, distribution and creator-revenue models.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Briefly attended KTH Royal Institute of Technology; left without a degree.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Subscription music services
strings.highlights.h1.text: Developed ad-supported and paid music streaming with co-founders and teams.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Platform economics and distribution debates
strings.highlights.h2.text: First annual profitability coexisted with debate over creator income, cost cuts and his external investments.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Becomes executive chairman
strings.timeline.t1.text: Left the CEO role; Alex Norström and Gustav Söderström became co-CEOs.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Helsing funding
strings.timeline.t2.text: His investment firm Prima Materia led a €600 million Helsing round, followed by protests from some musicians.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Announces first annual profit
strings.timeline.t3.text: Spotify reported its first profitable year, 2024, following subscriber growth, price increases and cost controls.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Announces roughly 17% layoffs
strings.timeline.t4.text: Ek explained staff reductions to lower costs and adjust the company’s size.
strings.timeline.t5.title: New York direct listing
strings.timeline.t5.text: Spotify entered public markets through a direct listing, not a conventional underwritten IPO.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Enters the US market
strings.timeline.t6.text: Spotify launched music streaming in the United States, expanding internationally.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Launches Spotify service
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began offering licensed music streaming in Europe.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Co-founds Spotify
strings.timeline.t8.text: Founded the company with Martin Lorentzon to develop an online-music business model.
